title: spec!: bound the remaining free-text payload members and state who reads them
body:
`SPEC.md` §7.3 item 19 has three parts. #296 closed most of part 1 across eight member names. This closes the rest of part 1 — **48 members** the name-based sweep did not reach — and does part 3, the half nobody had done.

## Part 1 — the remaining bounds

Sweeping every string subschema in `specs/**` that carries no `enum`, `const`, `pattern`, `format`, `$ref` or `contentEncoding`, then subtracting what item 19's own last paragraph excludes, leaves **48** unbounded free-text members across **27 draft specifications** and **10 shared schemas**.

The one the earlier review named specifically is here: `task-consent`'s `Effect.summary`, the member its own schema calls *"the ONLY member a consent surface is guaranteed to be able to render"*, was unbounded on the surface a human reads to approve an action. It is now 500 — the same figure as the `note` beside it.

| Bound | Members | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **64** | `webauthn` `rp.name`, `user.name`, `user.displayName`; `enroll-challenge` `rpName`, `userName`, `userDisplayName` | the length WebAuthn tells authenticators to truncate entity names to — a longer value is silently cut on the device rather than carried |
| **128** | `auth/challenge` `purpose`; `policy/activate` `Response.purpose`; `policy/active` `ActiveBinding.purpose`; `vtc/policies/test` `Response.purpose`; `vtc/ceremonies/list` `CeremonyManifest.purpose` | consistency repair, not a new judgement — `policy/activate` and `policy/active` already declared `maxLength: 128` on the **request** member while the response echoing it declared none |
| **256** | `deviceLabel` ×7, `Mention.displayName`, `AttachmentRef.filename`, `displayHint`, `CapabilityManifest.title`, `ContextRecord.name` + 3 context `name`s, `CommunityProfile{,View,Snapshot}.name` + `profile/update` `name`, `CeremonyManifest.blurb` | a display name, not prose — #296's own reasoning for `label`/`comment` |
| **500** | `Effect.summary`, `consequences[]`, `credential-exchange` `purpose` ×2, `deniedReason` ×2 | consent-surface prose a human reads while deciding — matches `task-consent/request/0.1` `note` |
| **1024** | `PolicyDecision.explanation` ×3, `Response.trace[]` ×3, `vtc` `error`/`lastError` ×3, `vta/credentials/issue` `purpose` ×2 | operator or service diagnostic prose |

Full list: 48 rows, `specs/**/payload.schema.json` and `specs/**/_shared/**`.

## Part 3 — who reads it, and whether it is retained

Item 19 also requires each specification to state **who reads** a free-text value, **whether it is retained**, and **whether it is trusted**. Prose is added to the `## Security & Privacy` section of all **37** draft specifications that reach a newly bounded member — the 27 whose own payload schema moved, plus 10 that reach one through a shared `$def`.

`task-consent/request/0.1` is the model, and its existing prose is extended rather than replaced. Elsewhere the paragraph says the same three things in the voice of the section it joins, e.g.:

> **Free text.** `deviceLabel` on each returned credential is free text, bounded at 256 characters. It was written at enrollment by whoever enrolled the credential — usually the subject, but an invited enrollment carries the *inviter's* suggestion — and nothing in the response attests to it. It is **untrusted** […] it is **retained** by the consumer for the life of the credential precisely so that this listing can show it.

**Remaining debt, stated plainly:** `vta/credentials/issue/0.1` and `0.2` had no `## Security & Privacy` section at all. They now carry one containing the item 19 statement, but **not** the four sub-headings the repo lint wants, so both stay on the Security & Privacy allowlist. The other 35 sections were extended in place; 5 of those (`chat/message`, both `credential-exchange`, `task-consent/request`, `vta/passkey-vms/enroll-challenge`) are full four-sub-heading sections from #295 and got their paragraph inside `### Data carried`.

## Deliberately untouched

Matching #296's own carve-outs, and item 19's last paragraph:

- **`messaging/_shared/0.1` `AuditEntry.detail`** and **`did-management/_shared/0.1` `DomainEntry.label`** — shared `$defs` reachable from a **retired** specification, so bounding them would move a frozen contract. Reachability was recomputed, not assumed: these are the only two shared schemas in this change's blast radius that a retired spec reaches. The ten this PR edits are draft-only.
- **All `retired` specs** (§5.3 freezes them) — 163 unbounded strings live there.
- **Not free text under item 19's own definition:** identifiers, opaque handles, digests, cursors and references; and values carried verbatim from an external vocabulary — DNS domains, `did:webvh` agent-name local parts, DID logs, Rego source, RFC 6901 pointers, HTTP header and cookie names, APNs topics, IANA media types, BCP 47 language tags, and maintainer- or community-defined `role`/`kind`/`provider`/`outcome` vocabularies.
- **`vtc/ceremonies/list` `nature` and `wired`** — the schema's own description names a closed set (`automatic | operator-driven | advisory`) that it never declares. A length is the wrong fix; the closed enumeration item 19 prefers is the right one, and that is a behaviour change for another PR.

## Still open — the "SHOULD be OPTIONAL" half

Not acted on here, as agreed: making a member optional is a wire-compatibility change.

**18 of the 48 bounded here are REQUIRED**, on top of the 13 #296 found — **31 in total**:

`CredentialCreationOptions` `rp.name` / `user.name` / `user.displayName` · `credential-exchange` `purpose` (query + deferred) · `Effect.summary` · `ContextRecord.name` + `vta/contexts/create` `name` · `enroll-challenge` `rpName` / `userName` / `userDisplayName` · `CommunityProfile.name` / `CommunityProfileView.name` / `CommunityProfileSnapshot.name` · `policy/activate` + `policy/active` + `vtc/policies/test` + `vtc/ceremonies/list` `purpose`

Several are required *by design* — purpose binding means a verifier cannot ask without saying why, and `Effect.summary` is the only member a consent surface is guaranteed to render — so the right outcome for those is for the specification to say so, not to change.

## Is item 19 closed?

**Part 1 and part 3 are closed for every `draft` specification.** What remains is: the two frozen `_shared` members above (reachable from retired specs — they close when those specs are superseded), the `retired` corpus itself (frozen by §5.3), the two `nature`/`wired` members that want an enumeration rather than a length, and the SHOULD-be-optional list.

## Breaking

Same terms #296 judged itself so. typify emits a bounded member as a validating newtype:

```diff
-    pub device_label: ::std::option::Option<::std::string::String>,
+    pub device_label: ::std::option::Option<PayloadDeviceLabel>,
```

```rust
if value.chars().count() > 500usize {
    return Err("longer than 500 characters".into());
}
```

Both halves break: the API a consumer compiles against moves, and a document the library previously accepted is now rejected. `@openvtc/trust-tasks` generates unchanged *types* — TypeScript has no length refinement — but its embedded schemas reject over-long values at runtime. Hence the `!`. **No version bumped, no changelog written** — release-plz computes both from the title.

## Verification

```
npm run validate     533 example documents re-checked; none rejected by a new bound
                     Security & Privacy: 42/349 full, 307 allowlisted, 0 not allowlisted
npm run build        Done.
npm run check-bindings  349 specifications vs 349 TS and 344 Rust modules — all agree
cargo build --workspace --all-targets   Finished (no call site broke)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets    39 suites, 0 failed
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   Finished
cargo fmt --all --check    clean
```

Changelog

## `trust-tasks-rs`

## [0.14.1](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/compare/trust-tasks-rs-v0.14.0...trust-tasks-rs-v0.14.1) — 2026-08-26 ### Added - **rs**: Make SPEC §7.3 item 17's issuedAt MUST expressible ([#300](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/300)) Framework 0.5.0's §7.3 item 17 says a Trust Task specification defining a consequential Trust Task MUST require the `issuedAt` member, raising §4.2's SHOULD to a MUST for documents conforming to it. There was no way to declare that: the meta-schema had `proofRequirement` for the `proof` envelope member and nothing equivalent for `issuedAt`, so the MUST was unexpressible and none of the 209 consequential specs in the registry could comply. Adds `issuedAtRequirement` to the front-matter meta-schema, modelled on `proofRequirement` — same two forms (a single `requirement`, or a per-variant `request`/`response` pair), same enum, same `rationale`. It governs an envelope member, admits a per-variant reading because request and response are relied on differently, and reading one declaration now teaches the other. Declared rather than derived, with the derived floor checked and reported: * `sideEffects` and `exposure` are DESCRIPTIVE (§7.3 items 13/14). Deriving `issuedAt`-REQUIRED from them would mean that correcting `sideEffects.level` from `none` to `mutating` for accuracy silently changed which documents every consumer of that spec must reject. * §2 makes the *handler* authoritative for consequentiality, not the front matter — so a value computed from the front matter would enforce something the front matter does not authoritatively state. * A non-consequential spec may legitimately require `issuedAt` anyway; a derived-only mechanism cannot express that. * Deriving would flip 209 specs' wire behaviour in one commit, invisibly. So the build derives the floor instead of substituting for the declaration. `npm run validate` prints a `Freshness floor (§7.3 item 17)` line counting the consequential specs that have not declared it (currently 0/209), *fails* on a spec that declares something weaker than REQUIRED, and escalates the undeclared case to a hard error under `TT_STRICT_ISSUED_AT=1` — the ratchet that becomes the default once the registry has caught up. Enforcement reaches consumers the same way `IS_PROOF_REQUIRED` does: * `Payload::IS_ISSUED_AT_REQUIRED` (Rust) and `SpecPolicy.isIssuedAtRequired` (TypeScript), emitted per variant by both generators from the front matter. * `TrustTask::enforce_spec_policy` / `enforceSpecPolicy` reject a document with no `issuedAt` as `malformedRequest`. Not `expired`: §8.3 defines no dedicated code, `expired` names a document that was once acceptable, and §7.2 item 13 already uses `malformedRequest` for the other freshness rejections. * The trait constant has a default of `false`, so hand-written impls — the crate's own `trust-task-error`, hand-modelled in `error.rs` because it is in the codegen's SKIP_SLUGS, and every downstream impl — keep compiling. * `check-bindings` compares the new key across front matter, Rust and TypeScript, so the two languages cannot drift on it. Distinct from `FreshnessPolicy::require_issued_at`, which is a *consumer's* own posture applied to every document it sees. This is the *specification's* requirement, published in the registry and not the consumer's to relax. No specification declares `issuedAtRequirement` yet — that is a follow-up, spec by spec. The generated Rust tree is therefore byte-identical (the const is emitted only on override) and the generated TypeScript gains one `isIssuedAtRequired: false` line per policy object. Nothing that was accepted before is rejected now. Also documents the declaration in CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md, and teaches `npm run new-spec` to emit it on a scaffold whose declared classes make the task consequential. ### Fixed - **rs**: Enforce both halves of the SPEC §6.1 slug reservation ([#293](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/293)) * fix(rs): enforce both halves of the SPEC 6.1 slug reservation TypeUri rejected a published framework specification and accepted a reserved one, in the same function pair: REJECTED trust-task-control published since 0.1; its Type URI would not parse PARSES trust-ceremony-evil reserved by 6.1, accepted from any party is_reserved_namespace checked only the trust-task half of ^trust-(task|ceremony)($|-|/), so the ceremony half of the reservation — which exists precisely so the ceremony layer has a namespace no other party can claim first — protected nothing. And is_allowed_framework_slug listed five slugs where specs/spec.meta.schema.json lists seven, so two published specs sat inside the reservation with no permission to be there. The allowlist is one of two hand-maintained copies. The new test reads the meta-schema's copy and fails naming the missing slug if they drift again; verified by removing trust-task-control and watching it fail. Found while retiring trust-task-ok ([#292](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/292)), which swept for references to the slug and noticed the two lists disagreed. ### Specifications - Bound every free-text payload member with a maxLength (§7.3) ([#296](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/296)) * spec: bound every free-text payload member with a maxLength SPEC.md §7.3 (framework 0.5.0) requires that any member holding free text declare a `maxLength`. 92 free-text string members across 83 draft schemas carried none, leaving the wire contract unbounded and every consumer to invent its own ceiling — or none, which is what §10.3 (schema-validation DoS) exists to prevent. Bounds are chosen per member from the vocabulary the registry already uses rather than applied uniformly: 256 `label`, `comment` — a display name or an OpenSSH key comment; matches the existing 256 on provision/integration `label` and the `name` members alongside it. 500 requester-authored prose that a surface renders to a human who is deciding something; matches task-consent/request/0.1 `note`, the registry's considered consent-surface bound. 1024 `reason`, `description`, `message` — operator or service prose recorded for audit or returned as a diagnostic; matches the six existing `reason: 1024` and the `description: 1024` in policy/ and vtc/endorsement-type. 16384 chat/message `text` — the task's actual content rather than metadata about it; matches the corpus's long-form bound on vault `secureNotes`. All amended specifications are `status: draft`, so the change is made in place per SPEC §5.2. Deliberately untouched: * 17 members in `retired` specifications, frozen by SPEC §6.4. * messaging/_shared/0.1 `AuditEntry.detail` and did-management/ _shared/0.1 `DomainEntry.label` — shared $defs reachable from a retired specification, so bounding them would change a frozen specification's effective wire contract. * vault/_shared/{0.1,0.2,0.3} `TspMessageEnvelope.message` — opaque base64url TSP bytes, not free text. The `label` description in vault/_shared/*/vault-entry.schema.json said the wire spec enforced no maximum length. It now does, so the sentence is corrected rather than left contradicting the schema it annotates. `npm run validate` re-checks all 533 fenced example documents against the amended schemas; none is rejected by a new bound. **No version has been taken for this entry yet, deliberately.** The change below is breaking under the rules at the top of this file, so releasing it moves the leading component and drags the six dependent crates with it — the workspace event the callout above says to plan rather than discover. Three specification PRs are in flight against the same registry; whoever sequences that cascade assigns the number and dates this heading. ### Changed - **BREAKING.** 92 free-text payload members across 83 draft schemas now declare a `maxLength`, which SPEC.md §7.3 requires of any member holding free text. Two consequences, both observable by a consumer: 1. **Type change.** A `String` member that gains a `maxLength` is generated by typify as a validating newtype, so `Option` becomes `Option`, `Option`, and so on. Reads through `Deref` are unaffected; construction and assignment are not. 2. **Behavioural change.** The newtype enforces its bound in `Deserialize`, so a document carrying an over-long value — one this library previously accepted — is now rejected. This is the "alters behaviour against an unchanged wire format" case named at the top of this file. #### Migration A builder setter takes the newtype rather than a `String`: ```rust // before let entry = grant::AclEntry::builder() .subject("did:web:carol.example") .role("moderator") .label("Carol — content moderation".to_string()) .try_into()?; // after let entry = grant::AclEntry::builder() .subject("did:web:carol.example") .role("moderator") .label(grant::AclEntryLabel::try_from("Carol — content moderation")?) .try_into()?; ``` The conversion is fallible precisely because the bound is real: a value longer than the schema permits now fails where it is authored rather than at the far end of the wire. Reading a member still derefs to `&String`, so `label.as_deref().map(String::as_str)` recovers an `Option<&str>`. Bounds were chosen per member from the vocabulary the registry already uses — 256 for a display `label` or an OpenSSH key `comment`, 500 for requester prose a surface renders to a human deciding something (matching `task-consent/request/0.1` `note`), 1024 for `reason` / `description` / `message`, and 16384 for a `chat/message` `text` body. Members in `retired` specifications are untouched, frozen by SPEC §6.4.
